sources.citation: Lithgow, David. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Para 29 (p.455) lists Waiema as a Taupota dialect. Sec. 84 'STRESS' (p.475) is family-wide only: 'There is a constant pattern of vowel lengthening near the end of the phonological word.. In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs. When a kinship noun is pluralised by the addition of a suffix, the stress moves one syllable closer to the end of the word.' Stress said to be phonemic only in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima (?Nimowa, Sudest). Nothing specific to Wa'ema/Taupota.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: Milne Bay Province. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 157-170. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C39.157 (hdl:1885/252993).
sources.note: No phonology of its own. Relevant pointers: (a) British New Guinea Annual Report 1893-94 contains a Wedau vocabulary (table of Annual Report wordlists, p.~160); (b) King 1901: 'There are only a few copies of Copland King's Wedau Dictionary still in existence, one or two being at Dogura. The grammar section is very brief, but the dictionary has about 3,000 Wedau words' (p.~165); (c) manuscript: 'Wedau 1947 Introduction to the Wedau Language by Canon JENNINGS, at Dogura' (p.166); no Taupota or Wa'ema manuscript is listed. Its only stress remarks concern other languages (Annual Report data and '…
Nothing on phonology; states Taupota is a dialect chain with southern varieties called Wa'ema and western Wedau.
